question: Which statement best reflects the WHO definition of palliative care?

answers.text: Palliative care begins only when curative treatment has failed and death is imminent

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The WHO definition explicitly states palliative care applies to life-threatening illness at any stage — not limited to the terminal phase. Early integration alongside curative therapy improves outcomes.

answers.text: Palliative care is an approach that improves quality of life of patients and their families facing life-threatening illness through prevention and relief of suffering

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The WHO definition encompasses physical, psychological, social, and spiritual dimensions of suffering — applicable alongside curative treatment, not only after it.

answers.text: Palliative care is equivalent to hospice care and focuses solely on the last weeks of life

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Hospice is a specific delivery model for end-of-life care. Palliative care is broader — it is applicable earlier in illness and alongside curative treatment.

answers.text: Palliative care refers exclusively to pain management and does not address other symptoms

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Palliative care addresses the full spectrum of suffering: pain, dyspnoea, nausea, anxiety, depression, spiritual distress, and family needs — not pain alone.

overallFeedback.feedback: Palliative care (WHO definition) addresses all dimensions of suffering in life-threatening illness from the time of diagnosis, alongside curative treatment — it is not limited to end-of-life or hospice settings.
Correct. The WHO palliative care definition emphasises comprehensive quality-of-life focus, applicable from diagnosis of life-threatening illness — not only at end of life.
